daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo addressed PKB's 28th anniversary celebration, declaring he will stop inflated government procurement prices and halt schemes causing budget leakage. The president told the audience that Indonesia's wealth has been taken abroad and vowed to fight those stealing the nation's resources, acknowledging some parties would be disturbed. Vice President Muhaimin Iskandar pledged PKB's continued support for Prabowo to advance his new economic direction.

  • The Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) searched the office and home of Lombok Barat regent, seizing financial records during the operation.
  • The DPR Speaker scheduled a meeting for next week to finalize the presidential regulation on ride-hailing services.
  • Prabowo told PKB attendees that Indonesia maintains good relations with all powers but Palestine's independence is non-negotiable.
  • The president praised PKB's political approach, suggesting founding figure Gus Dur might be watching from above.
  • Prabowo commented on PDI-P, saying the party's heart is actually the same as the government's.
  • The results of the ulama gathering were read out in President Prabowo's presence at the PKB event.
  • The Palace confirmed that appointing Nanik to the BGN supervisory board was the president's request, while a shadow cabinet criticized the appointment of Sudaryono to BGN.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia urged Japan and ASEAN to strengthen support for Palestine during regional diplomatic engagements. The Foreign Ministry announced Indonesia will replace China as a member of the UN Board of Auditors, marking a significant multilateral role. Indonesia also commended the UK's recognition of Palestine, welcoming the diplomatic development.

  • Indonesia called on the UK to assist ASEAN in combating online scam syndicates operating across the region.
  • The Foreign Ministry urged peaceful commitment in the South China Sea, with officials stating that incidents there underscore ASEAN's relevance.
  • Indonesia and Algeria signed a memorandum of understanding on pencak silat development to strengthen cultural diplomacy.
  • The Defence Ministry explained plans to purchase M-346F fighter jets, addressing speculation about the procurement.
  • Indonesia urged stronger ASEAN-China partnership amid regional uncertainty, while also prioritizing ASEAN-Russia partnership to strengthen community resilience and pushing for concrete ASEAN-EU cooperation.

Other

The government announced plans to establish Universitas Republik Indonesia, a new institution that will focus on STEM fields. However, the DPR's Education Commission stated that no explanation has been provided about the university's establishment, while a University of Indonesia law professor questioned the legality of the new institution.

  • Indonesia will mandate sustainable aviation fuel use beginning in 2027, marking a major environmental policy shift for the aviation sector.
  • The Finance Ministry plans to issue Panda Bonds as part of efforts to reduce dependence on the US dollar in government financing.
  • Coordinating Minister Airlangga stated that four countries are exempted from natural resource export proceeds regulations.
  • BRIN researchers uncovered traces of Majapahit city, discovering patterns of ancient settlements and wells.
  • The National Narcotics Agency (BNN) seized Rp165 billion in drug money laundering assets, while the government warned of a potential vape ban over drug abuse concerns.
